solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: RE prep's tricky to follow as written from right to left

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the turned word, following it in the answer
the little word as is to be set down backwards, the way Hebrew or Arabic script runs
something tricky is awkward and twisted, so the letters of prep's are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is taken as a letter here, giving P R E P S as fodder

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's homework for religious education is hard to follow, as if written in Hebrew.
explanation.walkthrough: RE looks like Religious Education beside 'prep' (homework), but it is the Royal Engineers; 'written from right to left' turns the little word round and 'tricky' jumbles the rest, which 'to follow' sets after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappers are soldiers of the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps abbreviated RE.

clue.text: Wicked cast in a new production

indicators.note: a new production of a play recasts and rearranges it, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A wicked cast has been assembled for a fresh staging of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new production' rearranges the letters of CAST IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, evil in the manner of Satan, a synonym for wicked.

clue.text: Hand father first fruit

indicators.note: the word for father is to be put first, ahead of the word for hand

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a paw is a jocular word for a hand

explanation.surface: Someone passes Dad the first piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaw, also spelt pawpaw or papaya, is a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Keep clear of Adam, getting short when his missus is around

indicators.note: the wife's name surrounds the shortened Adam, holding it within

parts.note: Adam's wife in Genesis is Eve; missus is slang for wife

indicators.note: Adam is cut short, losing its last two letters

explanation.surface: Avoid Adam, who turns curt whenever his wife is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting short' is a little generous here, as it removes two letters rather than one; 'is around' puts his wife's name round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade something is to dodge or avoid it, so it is a synonym for keep clear of.

clue.text: Toto in picture's a little tearjearker

indicators.note: the word for the whole is placed inside the word for a picture

parts.note: a shot is a photograph or picture
from the Latin phrase in toto, meaning wholly, toto is taken as all

explanation.surface: Toto, Dorothy's dog, appears in a film still, and the scene is a small weepie.
explanation.walkthrough: Toto suggests the dog from The Wizard of Oz, but here it is the Latin of 'in toto', meaning 'all'. The printed 'tearjearker' is a slip for tearjerker.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion, and cutting onions brings tears, so it is a little thing that jerks tears.

clue.text: Gadget combining revolutionary listening device with aid to vision

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word for the device is reversed

parts.note: a bug is a hidden microphone
bins is slang for binoculars

explanation.surface: A spy gizmo pairs a radical bugging device with a visual aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns BUG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gubbins is informal British slang for a gadget, gizmo or bits and pieces of equipment.

clue.text: Clothes chest with a number of shifts in it?

definitions.text: Clothes chest with a number of shifts in it?

parts.note: gear is informal for clothing
a box is a chest or trunk

explanation.surface: A wardrobe trunk holding several shift dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: A shift is an old word for a dress or chemise, so a clothes chest holds shifts; a car's gearbox holds the shifts between gears.
explanation.definitionFit: A gearbox is the casing of a vehicle's gears, through which the driver makes each shift of gear.

clue.text: Bed down? I'll drink to that!

parts.note: a bed, as of a river or sea, is its bottom
to down a drink is to sup it

explanation.surface: Is it time to turn in? A cheerful toast greets the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed down' looks like settling for the night, but splits into bed (bottom) and down (sup, drink).
explanation.definitionFit: Bottoms up is a drinking toast, said as glasses are raised, like cheers.

clue.text: Wacky fanzine about Leeds United forwards that's spread virally

indicators.note: the jumbled magazine letters go about, surrounding, the two initials
wacky means crazy and erratic, so the letters of fanzine are mixed up
forwards are the front players, so the front letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A zany football magazine about Leeds United's strikers goes viral online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wacky' scrambles the magazine word and 'about' wraps it round the two initials that 'forwards' takes. Leeds United is an English football club, and forwards are its attacking players.
explanation.definitionFit: Influenza, the flu, is an illness caused by a virus that passes from person to person.

clue.text: Be sulky, out of sorts, but tone suggesting sunny outlook?

indicators.note: being out of sorts means being upset or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is moody and grumpy, yet tries to adopt a cheerful tone of voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of sorts' rearranges BE SULKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky blue is a pale colour, the shade of a clear summer sky, so the tone hints at fine weather.

clue.text: UN secretary-general in a panto version?

definitions.text: UN secretary-general in a panto version?

indicators.note: the leader's surname sits inside the rearranged pantomime letters
a version is a reworked rendering, so the letters of a panto are rearranged

parts.note: Ban Ki-moon was Secretary-General of the United Nations from 2007 to 2016

explanation.surface: What would the head of the UN be called if he appeared in a pantomime?
explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a British Christmas pantomime stage show. 'version' rearranges the panto letters and 'in' places the surname inside; the whole clue doubles as a hint at a world leader's status.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is informal slang for the boss or most important person, which a secretary-general is.

clue.text: Strong drink said to be like grass, uneven

indicators.note: said signals that the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: strong tea could be called tough tea

explanation.surface: A potent beverage is described as rough and uneven like grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong drink' looks like spirits but is 'tough tea', which spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tufty describes something growing in tufts or clumps, as patchy, uneven grass does.

clue.text: Fish with no dressing reported to be Roosevelt's creation

indicators.note: reported signals the phrase is spoken, its sound giving the entry

parts.note: an undressed eel is a nude eel

explanation.surface: Roosevelt is credited with inventing a plainly served, unsauced fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no dressing' reads as no sauce on the fish, but means naked: a nude eel.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Deal was the programme of economic reforms that President Franklin Roosevelt introduced in the 1930s.

clue.text: Mix of blue iodine producing green liquid

indicators.note: a mix is a blend, so the letters are combined and rearranged

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Blending blue dye with iodine yields a green fluid in a chemistry experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder: 'Mix' rearranges OF, BLUE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Biofuel is fuel made from plants, and 'green' here means environmentally friendly.

clue.text: 007 endlessly following one vehicle with another — one's forgotten C-charge?

indicators.note: the trimmed agent's name comes after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the agent's name loses its final letter

parts.note: 007 is the code number of the fictional spy James Bond

indicators.note: the numeral one is forgotten, so left out of the second vehicle

parts.note: a taxi is another vehicle
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: James Bond trails a car in a cab, having forgotten to pay London's congestion charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BOND to BON; 'one's forgotten' drops I from TAXI. London's congestion charge is called the C-charge; C here is carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon tax is a levy on carbon emissions, a charge on C, the chemical symbol for carbon.

clue.text: Obscure, cryptic code written without silent letters or duplicates

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and scrambled, so the letters are rearranged
written loses its unsounded first letter and one of its two repeated letters

explanation.surface: A secret code, set down with no silent or repeated letters, stays mysterious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without silent letters or duplicates' removes W (silent) and one T from WRITTEN to give RITEN; 'cryptic' rearranges CODE plus RITEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means little known and abstruse, so it is a synonym for obscure.

clue.text: With complete control all round, treat opponent thus?

indicators.note: the two words for complete and control go round the letter for with

parts.note: over means finished, complete
the helm is the steering control of a ship

explanation.surface: With total command of the game, crush the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' sets the two words round the abbreviation. The wordplay itself describes overwhelming someone, which brings the clue close to an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm an opponent is to defeat them utterly, which is how one treats a rival with total control.

clue.text: Produce note to burn

parts.note: to sing is to produce a sound with the voice
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: To create a musical note is to scorch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'sing E': to produce a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to burn slightly, scorching the surface.

clue.text: Constant pain in store

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: There is a lot of persistent pain waiting ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store or hoard of goods.

clue.text: Fish box, where crates are stored

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A crate of fish sits in a warehouse where packing cases are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crates' looks like packing cases but is slang for old cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A car park is where vehicles, jokingly called crates, are left.

clue.text: Formula One substitute might be seen going round grid

definitions.text: might be seen going round grid

parts.note: Formula One motor racing is written F1, here read as FI
to replace is to substitute

explanation.surface: A replacement Formula One driver might be spotted lapping the starting grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grid' looks like the motor racing starting grid but is a grate, the metal frame for a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireplace surrounds the grate, a grid of metal bars that holds burning coal.

clue.text: Stuffed with soft bread (ends cut off) and raising agent?

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its final letter

parts.note: full means stuffed after eating
crumb is the soft inner part of a loaf

explanation.surface: A recipe stuffs something with soft breadcrumbs and adds yeast or baking powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising agent' looks like yeast in the kitchen, but means what lifts things. 'ends cut off' takes the last letters from FULL and CRUMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A fulcrum is the pivot on which a lever turns when lifting a load, so it helps raise things.

clue.text: Sheep's horn may be something deployed in defence

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a horn is a part of the ram's body

explanation.surface: A ram's horn might be used as a weapon to protect itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sheep's horn' as the ram's part.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive wall or embankment around a fort.

clue.text: Australian creature cruelly chained

indicators.note: treated cruelly, the letters of chained are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal from Australia has been chained up cruelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruelly' rearranges CHAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an egg-laying mammal native to Australia.

clue.text: Refreshment tent out of teas, I hear, after rector and wife got stuck into brew of ale

indicators.note: the remains of the tent come after the abbreviation for rector
the sounds are taken out of the word tent
I hear says the word teas is heard as letters, the two letter Ts

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like TT

indicators.note: the wife's abbreviation is lodged inside the stirred letters
a brew is a mixture, so the letters of ale are stirred

explanation.surface: The refreshment marquee has run out of tea, so the vicar and his wife start on the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refreshment' suggests food and drink but means renovation. 'I hear' turns teas into the letter Ts, which 'out of' removes; 'brew of' stirs the beer to EAL and 'got stuck into' puts the wife inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Renewal is the process of restoring or freshening something, a synonym of refreshment.

clue.text: Great having two parents of same gender — no hesitation

parts.note: two female parents: mam is a dialect word for mum, and mother

indicators.note: the hesitation sound is removed from the end of the second parent

parts.note: the second female parent is a mother

explanation.surface: Having two mothers is wonderful, without any doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no hesitation' removes ER, the sound of hesitating, from MOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means huge, enormous, which is a sense of great.

clue.text: Leader in Sun supporting principal source of power in the House

definitions.text: source of power in the House

indicators.note: in a down answer the letter sits beneath the word for principal, supporting it

parts.note: main means principal, chief

indicators.note: the leader of the word Sun is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A leading article in the Sun newspaper backs the main power base in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the House' looks like the House of Commons but means a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The mains is the main supply of electricity to a building, the source of household power.

clue.text: Uranium shown in former imperial measure

indicators.note: the chemical symbol is shown placed inside the word for former

parts.note: once means former, as in the once-great empire
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Uranium is displayed in an old imperial unit of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former imperial' suggests an old empire, but 'former' gives ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a unit of weight in the imperial system, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Privately, the way one would expect at first

parts.note: as means the way, as in do as I do
I'd is short for I would, one being I

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word expect

explanation.surface: Speaking privately, things went the way one would have anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark made privately, out of others' hearing, as on stage.

clue.text: Drunken Geraldine got straight again

indicators.note: drunken describes someone staggering, so the letters of Geraldine reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Geraldine, who had been drunk, sobered up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got straight' suggests sobering up but means put back in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Realigned means brought back into line, made straight once more.

clue.text: Shut up relative at the back of tower

indicators.note: the relative is placed behind the tower, at its back

parts.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle
a mum is a mother, a relative

explanation.surface: A relative is locked up behind a castle tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep mum is an idiom meaning stay silent, say nothing.

clue.text: Return item of value found round outskirts of Rome — a bit of mosaic

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the whole assembled piece is read in reverse
the asset word is found wrapped round the letters from Rome

parts.note: an asset is an item of value

indicators.note: the outskirts are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of Rome

explanation.surface: Bring back a valuable piece discovered on the edge of Rome: a mosaic tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found round' wraps the asset round the city's edges, giving ARESSET, and 'Return' then reverses the whole assembly, not just one part.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles or pieces of glass or stone used to make a mosaic.
